successors.name: Hittite Empire
successors.text: 'Around 1200 BC, the Hittite kings Tudhaliya IV and Suppiluliuma II waged military campaigns in Alashiya and forced its king to sign a treaty of submission'

ledger.x: c. 1400 BC (first dated mention): Alashiya is a land of its own. 'Around 1400 BC, the Hittite king Arnuwanda I chastised his vassal Madduwatta for raiding Alashiya.' The page gives no founding year and says only 'Middle and Late Bronze Ages'; the start is a bridging judgment at this earliest dated sentence. The Amarna…

c. 1200 BC: Alashiya submits to Hatti. 'Around 1200 BC, the Hittite kings Tudhaliya IV and Suppiluliuma II waged military campaigns in Alashiya and forced its king to sign a treaty of submission'; the Tudhaliya IV page has 'a statue was set up by Tudhaliya IV to commemorate his conquest of the Land of Alasiya' (reign…

c. 1200 BC (bridged): the kingdom of Alashiya ends in the record. No page opened gives its fate after the Hittite campaigns or the Sea Peoples; the end is drawn at the submission to avoid inventing a vassal period.

wars.name: Hittite campaigns in Alashiya
wars.outcome: Tudhaliya IV 'commemorate[d] his conquest of the Land of Alasiya' and, with Suppiluliuma II, forced its king 'to sign a treaty of submission' around 1200 BC.

certainty.note: The page does not say whether the kingdom covered all of Cyprus.
